title: Three Years and One Short Clock
subtitle: 日常生活 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 日常生活（人与自我·生活与学习·日常生活与作息）
meta: 主题语境：日常生活（人与自我·生活与学习·日常生活与作息）　|　核心词汇：night　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 night 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1960 the keeper ① kept the night that no traveller in the tower would have counted, and he said the keeping was the whole of the year. The ② night, meaning the evening itself and not the clock, ran three years and stayed uncounted in the book; a night, he said, is the only thing in a tower that is judged by how long it is left uncounted.

Every ③ night in that tower had the same short clock beside it, and the ④ night at the far stair, meaning the bell they kept for the children to ring and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A night, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to count; the keeper said the counting is the part that fills three years.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the night was the whole of the matter, meaning the rest and not the evening. The ⑥ night, meaning the rest and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody counts; night, he said, is either something you keep or the only word that means both an evening and a rest. He said the rest is the part they remember.

By 1965 the ⑦ night had become a line in a calendar, and the calendar had become an argument about the short clock. The ⑧ night of the whole thing, the keeper wrote in January, was one tower and three years of counting; night, he said, is either the bell at the far stair or the reason you learned to count. He said the counting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ night I remember is the evening counted in the calendar, which closed in 1967 and is still counted as the quietest in the tower. A ⑩ night, my mother said in 1969, is the only evening that improves by being counted; every night, she said, is a rest that has agreed to look like an evening. She said the rest was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 夜晚（指钟楼里每一个旁边的那一个）
B. n. 夜晚（指那个夜晚本身，与小小的座钟相对）
C. 固定搭配：keep the night 守这一个夜晚
D. n. 夜晚（指留给孩子们敲的那一口）
E. n. 夜晚之事（抽象总称，指一处钟楼的夜晚之事）
F. n. 夜晚（指年历里写到、被清点的那一个）
G. n. 夜晚、安歇（指一件事里人人都等却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 安歇（抽象总称，指人人都等却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: kept the night that no traveller in the tower would have counted
The night, meaning the evening itself and not the clock
the night at the far stair
the night was the whole of the matter
the night had become a line in a calendar
The night of the whole thing
A night, my mother said in 1969

answers.why: keep the night 意为“守这一个夜晚”，1960 年那位守夜人把钟楼里没有一位过路人肯清点的一个夜晚做了一遍。
night 意为“夜晚”，指那个夜晚本身而不是小小的座钟，它经过了三个年头而在簿子上没有被清点。
night 意为“夜晚”，指钟楼里每一个旁边的那一个，每一个旁边都有同一座小小的座钟。
night 意为“夜晚”，指最远那道旋梯的留给孩子们敲的那一口，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
night 意为“夜晚、安歇”，指一件事里人人都等却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这个安歇就是那件事的全部。
night 意为“安歇”，指人人都等却无人提起的那样东西而不是那个夜晚，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
night 意为“夜晚”，指年历里写到、被清点的那一个，到 1965 年这一个成了年历里的一行。
night 意为“夜晚之事”，守夜人一月写道，整件事的夜晚之事是一处钟楼和三个年头的清点。
night 意为“夜晚”，我记得的是年历里清点过的那一个，1967 年走完了，至今仍被说成钟楼里最安静的一个。
night 为抽象总称，母亲 1969 年说，夜晚是唯一会因为被好好清点而变得更好的夜晚。
